Merge Risk: Low · previous review 0e7b3
Keyboard users may be unable to see a full renamed filename before choosing a fix. The change is mergeable with that accessibility limitation acknowledged.
Security architecture risk: Minimal · up to 0e7b3
The change narrows an existing repair operation rather than granting new access. Exclusions are enforced during repair and rename planning, while existing workspace isolation, maintenance ownership and recovery behavior remain in place. No material security risk introduced or worsened by this change was identified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The relevant privileged outcome remains repair of the active workspace's library files, records and companions. The new payload can exclude scanner findings from an operation the renderer could already invoke; it does not select an additional workspace or supply a write destination. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — No introduced path-injection attack was identified in the exclusion flow. Renderer-supplied strings become set members and are compared against scanner-produced finding paths; filesystem operations continue to use the existing vault and scanned item identities. Malformed input may omit intended exclusions, but it does not grant additional filesystem authority. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The renderer-to-main trust transition remains behind the existing workspace-scoped request wrapper. The handler delegates the workspace stamp to the workspace gate, validates the exclusion payload separately, and invokes the same maintenance-controlled service operation.

CodeRabbit's outside-diff note on fa88d808 ("Keep long rename names reviewable"): partly taken in 0e7b35e9. Names stay on one line, as in the design: wrapping both columns doubles the row height and halves how many files fit before the list scrolls. Every truncated name, new name and note now carries a `title`, so the full text shows on hover.

CodeRabbit's nitpick on 0e7b35e9 ("Keep large finding groups responsive", trivial / heavy lift): not taken for now. Only the open group renders its rows, and a few hundred plain list items re-render well under a frame; virtualizing would also complicate the keyboard and screen-reader access the previous comment asked for. It reopens if a real vault with thousands of findings feels slow.
